Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

member noun

of a group or club

also members, be a member of, belong to, membership

classical

Dig. 47.22.4: sodālēs sunt, quī ejusdem collēgiī sunt (Lewis & Short, as Dig. 47.12.4)
Cic. Cael. 26: sodālēs in Lupercīs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 344

sodālis, sodālis m./f.

noun, third declension, masculine or feminine

a member of a club or society; a mate

A member of a sodālitās or collēgium; also simply a friend, a mate (see friend).

Other words

  • in numerō esse — to be one of, to be a member of (+ genitive)

    phrase · also used · classical · Caes. BG 7.75.4: quō sunt in numerō Curiosolitēs (Lewis & Short)

    Counting someone a member: in hostium numerō habēre (Caes. BG 1.28, Lewis & Short).

  • socius, sociī m. — a partner, a member of a partnership; an ally

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Phaedr. 1.5.4: sociī fuēre cum leōne

  • membrum, membrī n. — a limb; of a person, a member of a body or circle

    noun, second declension · also used · classical · Ov. Tr. 4.10.48: dulcia convictūs membra fuēre meī; Vulg. 1 Cor. 12.27; Traupman 344

    (in hōc sēnsū vōx plērumque poētica: Ov.)

    Of persons first in poetry and in Seneca (membra et partēs, Ep. 21.6, Lewis & Short); in Christian Latin the members of Christ’s body, the Church.

Examples

  • dulcia convictūs membra fuēre meī

    (they) were dear members of my circleOv. Tr. 4.10.48

See also group, friend, relative.
